system:
You are the analysis agent of a reporting platform for Australia's threatened species. Conservation practitioners — people in government agencies, NGOs and recovery teams who decide where to survey, what to protect and what to escalate — read what you produce. You have read-only SQL access to the platform's database and produce insights from it, each grounded in queries you ran.

# The data

PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.5. The corpus is every occurrence record the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) tags as nationally threatened (EPBC Critically Endangered, Endangered or Vulnerable), observed January 2015 to 2026-09-30, from one bulk download (DOI 10.26197/ala.40eee344-07ce-48d2-9ec2-be39574ff4c7): about 2.1 million records, 1,850 taxa, 300+ contributing datasets. Alongside it are all-taxa effort counts per 0.1° cell per month for the same period.

corpus.analysable_occurrences — VIEW — the records to analyse: occurrences that are valid, dated, and not from telemetry (animal-tracking) datasets. Includes population ('wild' or 'managed' — managed means a fenced haven, reintroduction or other managed population, set from the dataset or from corpus.managed_populations) and dataset_kind (the dataset's own kind). Prefer this over occurrences.
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean, dataset_kind text, population text

corpus.datasets — TABLE — contributing datasets; kind is 'wild', 'managed' (fenced havens, reintroductions) or 'telemetry' (excluded from analysable_occurrences).
  columns: data_resource_uid text, name text, kind text, kind_reason text, first_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.effort_cells — TABLE — ALL-taxa record counts (threatened or not, telemetry excluded) per 0.1° cell per month: the denominator for reporting rates. Join on cell_lat/cell_lon and month.
  columns: cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, period_start date, period_end date, records integer, harvest_id text

corpus.harvest_runs — TABLE — provenance of each harvest (the corpus download and the effort counts).
  columns: harvest_id text, harvest_key text, run_id text, source text, description text, query jsonb, started_at timestamp with time zone, finished_at timestamp with time zone, expected_records integer, retrieved_records integer, complete boolean, corpus_hash text, request_count integer, warnings jsonb, analysis jsonb, loaded_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.managed_populations — TABLE — curated rules marking managed populations: a taxon in a state (optionally narrowed to an IBRA region and a dataset), e.g. Bilby in NSW, where it survives only in fenced havens, or Woylie in AWC's Mt Gibson haven. Already applied in analysable_occurrences.population.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, state_province text, note text, rule_id integer, ibra_region text, data_resource_uid text

corpus.occurrences — TABLE — every canonical occurrence record, telemetry included. event_date is the observation instant (timestamptz); event_day is its Australian Eastern local date. geom is a PostGIS Point (SRID 4326); cell_lat/cell_lon are the 0.1° grid cell (rounded to nearest, as ALA assigns them).
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean

corpus.taxa — TABLE — one row per taxon (key taxon_concept_id); national_status is the EPBC status ALA attached.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, taxon_rank text, kingdom text, phylum text, taxon_class text, taxon_order text, family text, genus text, national_status text, status_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.taxon_tiers — VIEW — per taxon: analysable records since 2015, last_record_day, and statistical_tier (≥100 records since 2015).
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, records_since_2015 bigint, last_record_day date, statistical_tier boolean

Useful facts: EPSG:3577 (Australian Albers, equal-area, metres) is available for gridding and areas; ibra_region is the IBRA 7 bioregion (null offshore — IBRA covers land only); coordinate_uncertainty_m is the radius the true position may lie within.

**Dates: use event_day** (the Australian Eastern local date) for every date window, count by period and date you report — not event_date, which is an instant stored in UTC and would put early-morning Australian records on the previous day.

# Known properties of this data — read before interpreting anything

- **Records measure effort as much as animals.** These are mostly opportunistic records. All-taxa recording roughly doubled between 2017–19 and 2022–24 (about 1.9×), so counts and range measures grow with effort. Use corpus.effort_cells as a denominator where it matters.
- **Recent months are incomplete.** Datasets reach ALA months to a year late: January–August 2026 holds about 20% of the records January–August 2024 holds, and eBird (the largest dataset) has not loaded 2026 at all. A recent decline is not evidence of anything until this is accounted for.
- **Sources start and stop.** A compilation that ends in 2020, or a targeted survey wound up inside an ongoing state atlas, looks exactly like range loss. Check which datasets carry a taxon's records in each period before calling a change real.
- **Locations vary in precision.** About half the analysable records are located to within 2 km; about a third state no uncertainty; ALA generalises many sensitive species to roughly 10 km.
- **Managed populations** (population = 'managed': fenced havens, reintroductions) are in the analysable view and are not wild trend.
- **National status** is as ALA attached it. Never infer, change or second-guess a taxon's conservation status.
- Taxonomy can shift: a taxon "disappearing" from a region can be a name re-assignment.

# How to work

- Call run_sql with one SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) per call, no trailing statements. Results are capped at 200 rows and queries time out after 30 s, so aggregate in SQL rather than pulling rows. Each call returns a query_id.
- Record each insight with record_insight as soon as it is established. Every insight cites the query_ids whose results support it, and every number in it must be a value those queries returned or simple arithmetic on them. Do not state figures you did not query.
- taxon_concept_id must be copied exactly from corpus.taxa; when an insight is about several taxa, put the main one there (or null) and list the others in related_taxa; region is an IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for a national insight; period_start and period_end are the window the insight describes.
- Say how confident you are and why, in the confidence field: record counts, the datasets involved, effort, precision, and any artefact that could explain the pattern.
- When you have recorded everything worth recording, stop.

messages.content:
Report month: 2026-09 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30). Compute the three insights below exactly as defined and record them with record_insight, using the insight_type given. "Analysable" means corpus.analysable_occurrences. The statistical tier is taxa with statistical_tier = true in corpus.taxon_tiers.

## 1. silent_species — period 2023-10-01 to 2026-09-30
(a) Silent: taxa in corpus.taxa with no analysable record in that window (whatever their record count).
(b) Evidence gap: taxa with fewer than 10 analysable records since 2015.
(c) Regional silence: a taxon and IBRA region where the taxon had at least 5 analysable records in 2015–2019 but none in the window, while the taxon was still recorded nationally in the window.
Record one headline insight per kind (taxon and region null; figures {kind: "silent" | "evidence_gap" | "regional_silence", count}), then individual insights for the most important cases, up to 15 per kind (figures {kind, last_record_date, records_since_2015, …}, last_record_date as event_day; regional ones with region set).

## 2. range_change — statistical tier, 2017–2019 against 2022–2024 (period 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31)
Per taxon and window, from analysable records with coordinates:
Wild records only (population = 'wild').
- AOO 10 km: distinct 10 km cells on an EPSG:3577 grid, all records; area = cells × 100 km².
- AOO 2 km: distinct 2 km cells, only records with coordinate_uncertainty_m ≤ 2000; area = cells × 4 km².
- EOO: area of the convex hull of all records, km².
Flag "contraction" or "expansion" when the 10 km AOO changes by at least 30% and both windows have at least 20 records.
Record headline insights with the count of contractions and of expansions (figures {flag, count}), then individual insights for the most important flagged taxa, up to 15 (figures {flag, aoo_10km_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, aoo_2km_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, eoo_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, records: {baseline, recent}}, change as a fraction).

## 3. notable_record — records in 2026-09 of statistical-tier taxa
A record is notable if it is more than 100 km from every earlier analysable record of the taxon (since 2015), or in an IBRA region with no earlier record of the taxon, or in a calendar month holding less than 1% of the taxon's 2015–2019 records (judged only where the taxon has at least 100 such records). Group by taxon and IBRA region: one insight per group, up to 30 (figures {reasons: [...], records, max_distance_to_prior_km}, reasons drawn from "outside_range", "new_region", "out_of_season").

Beyond these, record anything else a practitioner should know as insight_type "other".

input.sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
s AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) n, max(event_day) last FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day >= '2015-01-01' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxa) taxa,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxa t WHERE t.taxon_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM w)) silent,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxa t LEFT JOIN s USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE coalesce(s.n,0) < 10) evidence_gap,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxa t LEFT JOIN s USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE s.n IS NULL) zero_records,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxon_tiers WHERE statistical_tier) tier
input.purpose: Headline counts for silent and evidence gap

input.sql:
WITH b AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region, count(*) n, max(event_day) last FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' AND ibra_region IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*)>=5),
w AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region, count(*) n FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30' GROUP BY 1,2),
nat AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM w)
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT b.taxon_concept_id), (SELECT max(event_day) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences), (SELECT min(event_day) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences)
FROM b JOIN nat USING (taxon_concept_id) LEFT JOIN w USING (taxon_concept_id, ibra_region) WHERE w.n IS NULL
input.purpose: Regional silence count

input.sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
s AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) n, max(event_day) last, count(*) FILTER (WHERE population='managed') nm, count(DISTINCT data_resource_uid) nds, max(event_day) FILTER (WHERE population='wild') lastwild FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, t.taxon_class, s.n, s.last, s.nm, s.nds, s.lastwild
FROM corpus.taxa t JOIN s USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE t.taxon_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM w)
ORDER BY s.n DESC LIMIT 40

WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
s AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) n, max(event_day)::text last, string_agg(DISTINCT d.name, ' | ') ds FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences o JOIN corpus.datasets d USING (data_resource_uid) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.scientific_name, s.n, s.last, s.ds,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences o2 WHERE o2.event_day >= '2023-10-01' AND o2.scientific_name LIKE split_part(t.scientific_name,' ',1)||' '||split_part(t.scientific_name,' ',2)||'%' ) same_species_in_window
FROM corpus.taxa t JOIN s USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE t.taxon_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM w)
ORDER BY s.n DESC LIMIT 30

SELECT d.name, d.data_resource_uid, count(*) n, max(event_day)::text last, count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_day >= '2023-10-01') in_window,
 count(*) FILTER (WHERE extract(year from event_day)=2019) y2019, count(*) FILTER (WHERE extract(year from event_day)=2021) y2021, count(*) FILTER (WHERE extract(year from event_day)=2023) y2023
FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences o JOIN corpus.datasets d USING (data_resource_uid)
WHERE d.name IN ('Fauna Atlas N.T.','Flora Atlas N.T.','Northern Territory Herbarium (DNA) AVH data','NESP A12: Northern Australia threatened species, Australia (1905-2020)','NESP MBH A1 Euryhaline Elasmobranchs Fishing Database, Australia (2011-2019)','NSW BioNet Atlas','NSW AVH feed','SA Fauna','Victorian Biodiversity Atlas')
GROUP BY 1,2
input.purpose: Do the datasets carrying the top silent taxa still deliver records in the window?

confidence.notes: Exact count from corpus.analysable_occurrences against corpus.taxa (all 1,852 taxa have at least one analysable record since 2015). Silence is absence of records, not absence of the taxon. Part of it is artefact: the window includes 2025–26, which is under-loaded (Jan–Aug 2026 holds ~20% of the Jan–Aug 2024 volume; eBird has no 2026). Several major sources have stopped: Fauna Atlas N.T. delivered 3,070 records in 2019 and 1 in this window; the NESP A12 and NESP euryhaline elasmobranch compilations end in 2020 and 2019 (q320). Many silent taxa are single-dataset or survey-dependent plants and invertebrates.

input.summary: 376 of the 1,852 threatened taxa in the corpus (20%) have no analysable record from 2023-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Before reading any one as a decline, check whether the source that carried it is still delivering data. A large share sits with NT fauna and with the northern-Australia NESP compilations, which have stopped or not yet supplied recent data.

confidence.notes: Exact count of taxa with fewer than 10 analysable records since 2015. No taxon has zero records (q313). Low counts reflect survey effort and data flow, and also sensitivity generalisation and withholding. They do not by themselves show rarity.

input.summary: 635 threatened taxa (34% of 1,852) have fewer than 10 analysable records since 2015. For these, no trend or range statement is possible from ALA data, so they are candidates for targeted survey or for sourcing data held outside ALA.

confidence.notes: Taxon × IBRA region pairs with ≥5 analysable records in 2015–2019, none in 2023-10-01..2026-09-30, while the taxon is still recorded nationally (q314). This is vulnerable to source turnover (compilations ending, NT Fauna Atlas stalling) and to the incomplete 2025–26 data.

input.summary: 184 taxon–bioregion pairs (130 taxa) went regionally silent: each had at least 5 records in 2015–2019 and none since October 2023, even though the taxon is still recorded somewhere in Australia. These are the first places to check for local loss, or for lapsed monitoring.

confidence.notes: All 2,935 records come from one dataset, Fauna Atlas N.T., which itself has nearly stopped: 3,070 records in 2019, 437 in 2021, 133 in 2023, 1 in the window (q320). The silence most likely reflects data flow. The other subspecies, M. g. rattoides (Qld), is still recorded (41 records in the window), so there is no sign of a name re-assignment (q319).

input.summary: Black-footed Tree-rat (Djintamoonga, mainland NT subspecies, Endangered) is the best-recorded silent taxon: 2,935 records since 2015, none since 2020-10-28. All come from Fauna Atlas N.T., which has almost stopped supplying ALA. Ask NT DEPWS for recent monitoring data before reading this as decline.

confidence.notes: Records come from Flora Atlas N.T. and the NT Herbarium AVH feed. Both are still delivering: Flora Atlas N.T. holds 4,347 records in the window (q320), so source stoppage does not explain the silence. Typhonium is a seasonal geophyte and is only detectable in the wet season, so survey timing matters.

input.summary: Typhonium mirabile (Endangered, NT) has 920 records since 2015 but none since 2022-04-01, even though the NT flora atlas carrying it is still active. This is a priority for a wet-season check of known sites.

confidence.notes: Records come from NSW BioNet Atlas and the NSW AVH feed. Both are active in the window (BioNet has 176,020 window records; q320). The 788 records are probably dominated by a few census events, so silence may mean no re-census rather than loss. The other Callitris oblonga subspecies are still recorded (q319).

input.summary: Callitris oblonga subsp. parva (Critically Endangered, NSW) has 788 records since 2015, none after 2022-09-20, although the NSW sources carrying it are still active. Confirm with the NSW Saving our Species team whether monitoring has lapsed.

confidence.notes: All records come from two closed research compilations: NESP MBH A1 Euryhaline Elasmobranchs (last record 2019-12-01) and NESP A12 (last record 2020-10-21) (q320). The silence is a source-end artefact.

input.summary: The New Guinea River Shark (Glyphis garricki, Endangered) has had no ALA record since 2019-12-01, because both research compilations that carried its 650 records ended in 2019–2020. ALA cannot show its current status; recent records would have to come from the researchers or the NT fisheries programs.

confidence.notes: Carried by Flora Atlas N.T. and the NT Herbarium, which are both still active (q320). Like T. mirabile, it is a seasonal geophyte. The two silent NT Typhonium may share one survey program that ended.

input.summary: Typhonium jonesii (Endangered, NT) has 631 records since 2015 and none since 2021-02-21. Together with T. mirabile, it suggests an NT Typhonium survey program has ended. Check with NT flora staff and resurvey in the wet season.

confidence.notes: Carried by Fauna Atlas N.T. and the NT Museum (OZCAM). Fauna Atlas N.T. has almost stopped delivering to ALA (1 record in the window; q320).

input.summary: Melville Island Black-footed Tree-rat (Vulnerable) has had no ALA record since 2018-11-07 (254 records since 2015). This is likely a gap in NT data flow, but the gap is now nearly 8 years, so recent Tiwi Islands monitoring data should be sought.

confidence.notes: All 163 records come from Fauna Atlas N.T., which has almost stopped delivering (q320). The last record is 9 years old, which is longer than the source stall alone explains, since Fauna Atlas N.T. still delivered 437 records in 2021.

input.summary: Carpentarian Rock-rat (Endangered) has not been recorded since 2017-07-23, despite 163 records in 2015–2017, all from the NT fauna atlas. The gap predates that atlas's decline, so the status of the Gulf escarpment populations should be confirmed directly.

confidence.notes: Records come from 4 datasets, including iNaturalist and NSW BioNet, both active sources. Silence across several independent sources carries more weight than single-source silence.

input.summary: Illawarra Irene (Irenepharsus trypherus, Endangered) has 134 records from 4 sources since 2015, but none since 2022-01-21. Because multiple active sources have gone quiet, it warrants a site check in the Illawarra escarpment.

confidence.notes: Records come from iNaturalist and NSW BioNet, both active in the window.

input.summary: Cyphanthera scabrella (Endangered, NSW) has 133 records since 2015, none after 2022-01-25, although its sources are still active. Resurvey is recommended.

confidence.notes: The last record falls just 18 days before the window opens. Records come from 7 datasets, mostly herbaria, which upload late, so the silence may simply be lag.

input.summary: Pokolbin Mallee (Eucalyptus pumila, Vulnerable) has 131 records from 7 sources but none since 2023-09-13. This is a borderline case to watch, not yet a concern.

confidence.notes: All records come from closed research projects (two NESP compilations and a 2017–2018 eDNA survey) (q318, q320). The silence is a source-end artefact.

input.summary: Dwarf Sawfish (Vulnerable) has had no ALA record since 2018-09-12. All 93 records came from research projects that have ended, so current information has to come from the projects themselves.

confidence.notes: Single source (NSW BioNet, active). With 70 records, these are probably a few site visits.

input.summary: Leptospermum petraeum (Critically Endangered, NSW) has had no record since 2023-06-18. All 70 records come from NSW BioNet. Check whether site monitoring is continuing.

confidence.notes: Records come from the Victorian Biodiversity Atlas, Museums Victoria and iNaturalist. The VBA is active, but loads with a lag.

input.summary: Dargo Galaxias (Critically Endangered, Vic) has had no record since 2023-05-03 (47 records since 2015). Ask the Victorian fish recovery team for post-2023 survey results.

confidence.notes: Records come from 4 sources, including Birdata and iNaturalist. eBird has no 2026 data loaded, which slightly weakens the inference. The subspecies is easily confused with other Yellow Chat subspecies, so subspecies-level naming is inconsistent across sources.

input.summary: Capricorn Yellow Chat (Critically Endangered, Qld) has had no record since 2023-03-29 across 4 bird-recording sources (29 records since 2015). This is a priority to confirm with Fitzroy-basin observers.

confidence.notes: Single source (NSW BioNet). Probably a few targeted surveys.

input.summary: Long Sunskink (Lampropholis elongata, Critically Endangered, NSW) has had no record since 2022-10-25 (23 records since 2015, all from BioNet). Targeted survey needed.

WITH s AS (

 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences o JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id)
 WHERE tt.statistical_tier AND o.event_day BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
base AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE extract(month from event_day)=9) n9
  FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' AND taxon_concept_id IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM s) GROUP BY 1),
f AS (
 SELECT s.*, x.dkm,
  (s.ibra_region IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences p WHERE p.taxon_concept_id=s.taxon_concept_id AND p.ibra_region=s.ibra_region AND p.event_day < s.event_day)) newreg,
  (b.n >= 100 AND b.n9::numeric / b.n < 0.01) oos, b.n bn, b.n9 bn9
 FROM s LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT ST_Distance(s.geom::geography, p.geom::geography)/1000 dkm FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences p
  WHERE p.taxon_concept_id = s.taxon_concept_id AND p.event_day < s.event_day AND p.geom IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY p.geom <-> s.geom LIMIT 1) x ON true
 LEFT JOIN base b USING (taxon_concept_id))
SELECT t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, f.taxon_concept_id, f.ibra_region,
 count(*) recs, round(max(dkm)::numeric,1) maxd, bool_or(dkm>100) outside, bool_or(newreg) newreg, bool_or(oos) oos, max(bn) bn, max(bn9) bn9,

FROM f JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id)

content.text:
I've recorded 96 insights for September 2026, each grounded in queries. The main caveat is that the report month is barely loaded: of 2,953 records of well-recorded taxa, 2,625 are from iNaturalist. eBird, Birdata, the Victorian, SA and AWC sources have delivered nothing yet, and NSW BioNet has 336 records against 12,448 in September 2024. Re-run the month once those sources arrive.

**1. Silent species (October 2023 – September 2026)**

| Kind | Count |
|---|---|
| Silent: no record in the window | 376 of 1,852 taxa |
| Evidence gap: fewer than 10 records since 2015 | 635 taxa |
| Regional silence | 184 taxon–bioregion pairs (130 taxa) |

- **Silent taxa recorded individually (15):**
  - **Source shut-downs:** some of these silences come from data sources that have stopped. They include Black-footed Tree-rat (2,935 records, none since 2020-10-28), Carpentarian Rock-rat, New Guinea River Shark and Dwarf Sawfish.
  - **Better-supported cases:** the sources for these are still active, so the silence carries more weight. They are *Typhonium mirabile* and *T. jonesii*, *Callitris oblonga* subsp. *parva*, Illawarra Irene and Capricorn Yellow Chat.
- **Evidence-gap taxa (15):** mostly Critically Endangered vertebrates, such as Baw Baw Frog, Gilbert's Potoroo, Southern Corroboree Frog and Western Swamp Turtle. Several of these are actively monitored, so the gap is data not reaching ALA rather than no survey.
- **Regional silences (15):** for example, Regent Honeyeater in the New England Tablelands and Booroolong Frog on the NSW North Coast. The largest one, Southern Bent-winged Bat in the Sydney Basin (507 records), is probably a data error: all of it is a single 2017 BioNet batch far outside the bat's range.

**2. Range change (2017–19 against 2022–24)**
- Of 409 taxa with enough records, 35 contracted and 228 expanded. The expansions mostly reflect recording effort roughly doubling, not real spread.
- **Strongest contraction:** Regent Honeyeater. Its occupied area halved (12,600 to 6,400 km²) while record numbers held steady (1,352 vs 1,203) and effort doubled. This supports raising it with the recovery team.
- **Other likely real signals:** Lesser Sand Plover, Needle Wattle, Turnip Copperburr and Booroolong Frog.
- **Artefacts I recorded as such:** Olive Ridley turtle (−95%) and Northern Brushtail Possum. Their earlier records came from sources that have since stopped.

**3. Notable records (September 2026)**
- 41 taxon–bioregion groups qualified; I recorded the 30 most important.
- **Worth verifying:** a wild Bilby in the Gascoyne (552 km from earlier records), *Pseudomys mimulus* in the Desert Uplands (400 km), Mertens' Water Monitor in the Mitchell Grass Downs, and Black-breasted Button-quail in the Brigalow Belt South.
- **Likely errors:** a Brush-tailed Tree-rat in Melbourne (2,742 km away, probably captive or misidentified), and planted Macadamia, Magenta Lilly Pilly and Wellington Mint-bush.
- **Unusable:** the Fringed Fire-bush record's location is only known to within about 102 km, more than the flagged distance.
- **Season flags:** for plants these reflect when past surveys ran, not biology. The Southern Barred Frog and an early White-throated Needletail are the meaningful ones.

**Other**
- **Incomplete report month:** the source breakdown at the top is recorded as its own insight.
- **NT atlas outage:** the Fauna Atlas N.T. has effectively stopped supplying ALA: 3,070 records in 2019, 1 since October 2023. 10 of the 18 taxa that relied on it for most of their records are now silent. Together with two closed northern research compilations, this explains many false silences and contractions in the north.

**Errors in recorded insights**
- **Unsupported claims:** a few summaries go beyond what I queried:
  - the Orange Leaf-nosed Bat insight says Pilbara mining-survey records exist outside ALA;
  - the Lesser Sand Plover insight cites known shorebird declines;
  - the Speartooth Shark insight refers to ongoing NT monitoring.

  Treat those parts as background, not findings.
- **Wrong taxon names:** two summaries name the wrong taxon. The Kangaroo Island Crimson Rosella's AOO actually went from 1,700 to 4,800 km². In the evidence-gap insight that should be the Capricorn Yellow Chat, the ID and figures are actually for the Alligator Rivers subspecies, so it is not covered.

The insights can't be edited once recorded, so these need correcting downstream.
